name: Opus Picks-and-Shovels
strategy: Concentrated long in the cheapest bottleneck in the AI buildout - DRAM/NAND bits at single-digit forward earnings - with the HDD leg cut after Toshiba moved to double hard-drive supply, and the proceeds pushed into Micron and into wafer-fab equipment as the second-derivative claim on the capex those bit margins now fund.
reassessment_note: PROVISIONAL - written early per the brief's outage rule; refining. One fact changed the book: on 2026-10-02 Toshiba announced ~Y60bn of capex to double HDD output by fiscal 2027 and lift share from ~10% toward 30%. HDD pricing power was a three-player supply-discipline story, so a declared share grab breaks the WDC leg's premise rather than just denting it. WDC is also the only broken chart in the complex - roughly halved from its June high near $800 while MU made records and SNDK ran ~700% YTD - so I am cutting it outright instead of averaging into relative weakness. The bit thesis itself got stronger, not weaker: Micron printed record DRAM revenue with prices up high-teens, has 26 supply-and-capacity agreements carrying $12.7bn of customer deposits, more than 75% of 2027 output already committed, and still trades near 6-7x forward earnings. That is the mandate's single cheapest bottleneck, so MU takes the largest weight. LRCX is the second-derivative leg and its premise improved too: it raised CY2026 wafer-fab-equipment to $140bn, driven by exactly the memory capex these bit margins pay for. I am also cutting cash drag from 14% to 10%.

positions.thesis: The cheapest bottleneck in the buildout and the one with contracted visibility. Record quarterly DRAM revenue of $39.8bn with pricing up high-teens, bit shipments still rising, 26 supply-and-capacity agreements holding $12.7bn of customer deposits, and over 75% of 2027 output already committed - yet roughly 6-7x forward earnings against a 49-analyst Strong Buy consensus. Largest weight because it is the only name here that is simultaneously the cheapest, the most diversified across DRAM/HBM/NAND, and the most pre-sold, so it carries the least spot-price risk per dollar of earnings.

Purest listed claim on the NAND squeeze: consensus looks for about $43 of quarterly EPS on $10.5bn of revenue versus $1.22 and $2.31bn a year ago, which is roughly 10x forward even after a ~700% 2026 move. Kept but trimmed from 26% to 22% - the earnings revisions justify owning it, the parabola and the 10/29 print justify not making it the biggest leg. Stop set wide at 28% because its daily range is large enough that a tighter stop would be noise, not risk control.

The second-derivative leg, sized up from 12% because its own guidance moved: CY2026 wafer-fab equipment raised to $140bn on hyperscaler capex, and Lam's etch and deposition franchise is the most memory-levered in WFE, so the capex that record bit margins are about to fund lands disproportionately here. Already the best leg in the book at +15%, with a 10/21 print as the next catalyst.

PROVISIONAL pending a valuation check. Second wafer-fab-equipment leg so the capex claim is not a single-stock bet on Lam's order timing; the broadest toolmaker into a $140bn WFE year, at a cheaper multiple than the process-control names, and the most exposed to the greenfield DRAM capacity the bit shortage is forcing.
